name: cursing stones

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cursing stones are an Irish ritual object. Small round stones sit in a graveyard or another sacred site. People believe the stones carry a curse farther and faster. The stones also make the curse stronger than a bare spoken curse. A specific ritual often attaches to their use. At Ballysummaghan and Baroe in County Sligo the curser must go barefoot. Undoing a curse is hard, if not impossible. At Sligo the cursed person must agree to be buried for a while. During that time helpers recite charms against the curse. At Kilmoon in County Clare, between Killeany and Lisdoonvarna, famous stones led to a murder. In the eighteenth century a victim seemed to be turning the stones against his attacker.

okr.objective: Cursing stones are Irish stones that strengthen a spoken curse.
